messages:
maria: Heads-up — since the cilium 1.19 rollout around 04:00 UTC we're seeing 4-9% packet loss on west2 GPU cluster, mostly pod->pod (east-west). Training jobs are timing out. Not CPU or GPU constrained. Anyone seen this pattern after 1.19?

santiago: Which AZs / node pools? tunnel or host-routes?

maria: Mostly across az-a <-> az-b on the gpu-pool autoscaled nodes. We run geneve tunnels. MTU on pods still 1450. Kernel logs have a lot of GSO/TSO warnings.

kevin: We did push cilium 1.19.0 -> 1.19.2 last night (config drift). There was an internal change to tunnel fragmentation handling. Could be related.

ryan: Can you paste a short tcpdump and iperf sample? Also NIC RX/TX error counters?

maria: pasted quick captures, truncated:
```
14:12:03.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0) 10.2.5.12 > 10.3.6.8: UDP, length 1500
14:12:03.123457 IP (frag 1234) > fragment 1/?.
14:12:03.123460 IP (tos 0x0) 10.3.6.8 > 10.2.5.12: UDP, length 1200
```
and dmesg shows repeated: `geneve: frag failed, mtu mismatch` and `gso: packet too large, dropping`

iperf between pods (10s):
```
[  4]  0.0-10.0 sec  850 MBytes  714 Mbits/sec  6.8% packet loss (sawtooth pattern)
```

maria: loss pattern oscillates roughly every 25-35s — looks like batching/flush interval interaction.

santiago: sounds like tunnel fragmentation + GSO interaction. Did we change kernel flags or MTU defaults in the cilium configmap?

kevin: cilium-config was patched to enable "autoMTU=true" for canary but the default tunnel-mtu fallback changed in 1.19.2 — seems we missed adjusting host MTU on gpu-pool nodes. Also noticed RDMA-enabled nodes got geneve encapsulation incorrectly applied for a subset.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] cilium upgrade to 1.19.2 completed on cluster-west2 at 2026-03-18T04:11:34Z

ryan: Quick mitigation: reduce tunnel MTU to 1300 and enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on hosts; that should avoid large fragmented packets. Also try disabling GSO offload for geneve temporarily.

maria: patching cilium configmap now (kingdom of kubectl):
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm cilium-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"tunnelMTU":"1300","bpf-gso":"false"}}'
```
Applying to canary node pool first.

kevin: I'll prepare rollback manifest for 1.18.5 in case mitigation doesn't hold. We want minimal blast radius — start with 10% canary.

santiago: Also set on hosts: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and lower the NIC offload for GSO on the affected machines: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off` (schedule during low traffic).

maria: Canary patch applied to gpu-canary (4 nodes). Monitoring now.

(10m pass)

maria: Update: packet loss dropped to ~0.6% on canary nodes, training retries reduced. Still seeing occasional microbursts but much improved.

kevin: Good. I'll hold the rollback unless it creeps up again. Need a postmortem and checklist: audit cilium-config changes, validate geneve MTU handling in 1.19.x, and ensure RDMA node-labels skip tunnel encapsulation.

ryan: I'll add an automated probe for pod->pod iperf across AZs to catch the sawtooth pattern early.

maria: Filing incident and scheduling a follow-up on diagnostics + permanent fix (either stable MTU negotiation in cilium or explicit host MTU enforcement). Will tag infra-sre and eng-runtime.

sre-oncall: Thanks for the quick actions. Add links to any logs in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

kevin: Action items: 1) Roll forward mitigation cluster-wide if stable 2) PR for cilium-config defaults to enforce tunnelMTU for gpu-pool 3) Test RDMA label path 4) Postmortem with timeline.

maria: Agree. I'll continue monitoring and report in #incidents once postmortem is up.
